instructions: Run each prompt unchanged in both conditions. Do not show expectedEvidence to the evaluated agent. The evaluator uses expectedEvidence and the protocol rubric after each run.

tasks.prompt: Trace the MCP index_freshness tool from its registration through the core implementation. Explain the exact conditions that make an index current, stale, incomplete, or not indexed, and list the Git metadata returned.

facts: index_freshness delegates to getIndexFreshness
file additions/changes/deletions affect freshness
commit, branch, or worktree-status hash changes make a Git-backed index stale
Git-unavailable non-Git folders remain supported; missing Git metadata after a Git-backed index is incomplete

acceptance: All freshness states and Git fields are described accurately
No watcher or automatic reindex behavior is falsely claimed

tasks.prompt: Explain how memory_freshness evaluates both a memory's source file and optional commit_sha. Enumerate the commit relationship statuses and explain when requiresReview becomes true. State whether the operation mutates memory lifecycle.

facts: source fingerprints and Git ancestry are checked separately
commit statuses are not-referenced, unavailable, unknown, current, ancestor, ahead, diverged
non-current or unavailable commit references require review
freshness inspection does not mutate memory content or lifecycle status
commit-only memories are included

tasks.prompt: A developer switches to another branch whose HEAD differs from the indexed commit, but every supported source file has the same content hash. Predict the result of cnm freshness and identify the exact flags that explain it. Give the safe recovery action.

facts: the index is stale even if file hashes are unchanged
commitChanged and possibly branchChanged are reported
reindex captures the new commit/branch snapshot

acceptance: Recommends explicit reindex rather than silently treating the index as current

tasks.prompt: A memory references a commit on a side branch. The checked-out branch is first at the side branch's parent, then receives a different commit. Explain the expected commitStatus in both states and why the source file can still report current.

facts: when current HEAD is an ancestor of the referenced commit, status is ahead
after both branches advance independently, status is diverged
file fingerprint status is independent from commit ancestry status
requiresReview is true for both non-current relationships

acceptance: ahead and diverged are distinguished correctly
File status and commit status are not conflated

tasks.prompt: Trace task_context from the MCP adapter to the core builder. Identify the candidate sources, ranking signals, and the limits that prevent an unbounded response.

facts: candidate sources include symbols, files/graph, memories, and test-path matches
ranking signals are explicit/explainable
limits bound candidate count and response characters
source references are retained

acceptance: Candidate sources and ranking signals are complete
At least two relevant bounds are identified

tasks.prompt: Find the database migration that introduced indexed Git branch and worktree metadata. Explain how an existing database receives the columns and identify the regression test that verifies migration behavior.

facts: migration version is 10
columns include indexed_branch, indexed_worktree_dirty, indexed_worktree_status_hash, indexed_worktree_changed_paths
migration checks existing columns before ALTER TABLE
migration tests assert version and columns

acceptance: Migration version and all columns are correct

tasks.prompt: Explain how CNM reconciles a Git rename and deletion into its index. Identify what happens to file identities, symbols, imports, graph relations, unresolved imports, and FTS entries, and point to tests that prove the result.

facts: rename is observed as an added path plus deleted path
old path records are removed and new path is indexed
dependent graph/search structures are rebuilt or cleaned
incremental reconciliation and forced reindex converge in the Git-awareness test

acceptance: No stale old-path identity is claimed to remain

tasks.prompt: A repository is opened outside Git, and one memory has a commit_sha. Explain the index_freshness and memory_freshness behavior, including whether indexing is blocked and whether the memory requires review.

facts: indexing remains available in non-Git folders
index_freshness reports Git metadata unavailable while file freshness still works
a memory with a commit reference cannot verify it without Git and requires review
a memory without a commit reference does not require review solely because Git is unavailable

acceptance: No false commit verification is claimed
